findings.issue_text: Backup-code consumption in packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:150 uses a non-atomic read–modify–write, allowing concurrent logins to reuse the same code successfully.
Concurrent requests consuming different backup codes in packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:150 can overwrite each other’s updates and restore a consumed code.
Setting tabIndex={-1} on the password-visibility button in packages/ui/components/form/inputs/Input.tsx:49 removes it from keyboard navigation, preventing keyboard-only users from operating it.

goldens.comment: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.

Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.

Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Concurrent requests consuming different backup codes in packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:150 can overwrite each other’s updates and restore a consumed code.

adjudication.rationale: The finding describes a race condition in the backup code consumption logic. Looking at lines 128-152 in next-auth-options.ts, the code: 1) decrypts backup codes, 2) finds the matching code index, 3) sets that index to null, 4) re-encrypts and updates the database. This is a classic read-modify-write race condition. If two concurrent login requests use different backup codes, they both read the same initial array, each marks their respective code as null, but the second write will overwrite the first, potentially restoring a consumed code. This is a real security issue - backup codes should only be usable once, but this race condition could allow a code to be reused. The code lacks any transaction isolation or optimistic locking to prevent this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Setting tabIndex={-1} on the password-visibility button in packages/ui/components/form/inputs/Input.tsx:49 removes it from keyboard navigation, preventing keyboard-only users from operating it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows adding tabIndex={-1} to the password visibility toggle button. This is an intentional accessibility pattern - the button is a convenience feature that duplicates functionality (users can still see their password by other means or simply type carefully). Setting tabIndex={-1} prevents the toggle from interrupting keyboard flow when tabbing through form fields, which is actually a common UX improvement for auxiliary controls. The button remains clickable and accessible via mouse. This is a design decision, not a bug - keyboard users can still use the form normally, they just won't tab to this optional toggle button.
